result:
Round 82 is implemented: clip fade in/out (SRW-18 stage 1) and X1, the clearer status after a refused lane drag. All checks I ran pass. The code-reviewer found a double-click bug that I confirmed in real Chromium and fixed. The audio rows (export ratios, live meter) are not verified in a browser yet; that is C's round. Nothing is committed. The full report is in `tmp/studio-real-loop/a-round-82.md`.

**What changed** (12 files, 8 modified + 4 new, all inside the B grant; frozen list 467/467 and protected files 4/4 still match):
- **Model and edits:** clips have optional `fadeIn` / `fadeOut`, and fade-in plus fade-out can never exceed the clip length. Moves, duplicates and copy/paste keep fades. Trim shrinks the fade on the trimmed side first. Split, Delete Time, Delete/Cut on a range, and range copy drop the fade at each new cut.
- **Audio:** playback and export both put a separate fade gain node before the clip gain, so a live Clip Gain change cannot disturb the fade. A clip without fades builds exactly the old graph. The context change is one line plus its import.
- **Handles:** two small handles under the clip header. Dragging writes one `Fade In` / `Fade Out` undo entry, a cancelled or lost pointer reverts, and double-click resets the fade to 0. They appear on hover, on a selected clip, or when the fade is above 0, and never on video clips, folded lanes or clips narrower than 24 px.
- **X1:** a drag released on an occupied lane now says where the clip stayed, e.g. `აქ ადგილი არ არის — კლიპი ბოლო თავისუფალ ადგილას დარჩა: მუსიკა, start 00:01.375.` Where it ends up is unchanged.
- **Docs:** doc 070 l.72 and doc 071 l.4 updated as granted; new doc 072 in Georgian.

**Checks I ran:**
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` and scoped Biome on the owned files are clean.
- 74 targeted test files, 1366 tests, pass (72 existing + 2 new), with no existing test turning red.
- All 8 required mutations (a)–(h) turn their tests red on the final code. Three more (i)–(k) undo each review fix and also turn red.
- In my own Chromium check (not C evidence), a real +40 px handle drag gave a 1.000 s fade with the right status. A real double-click left it at 1.000 before the fix and reset it to 0.000 after.

**Review (7/10):**
- **H1, double-click:** a real double-click never reached the handle; the fade drag now holds the pointer on the handle itself.
- **M1, meeting fades:** when the two fades met exactly, float rounding could silence the fade-in and then jump; now guarded and tested.
- **M2, overlapping handles:** a fade-in handle could be stuck under a fade-out handle that can't move; an active handle now sits on top.
- **Smaller fixes:** a 2 px border offset on the fade-out handle, three missing test cases, and two inaccuracies in doc 072.
- **Not fixed:** hidden handles still catch presses at the clip's top corners and don't handle touch drags (the trim strips behave the same), and a minor fades-module edge case no code reaches.

I did not send the fixes back for a second review; each fix has a test that turns red when the fix is undone. The reviewer's Architecture note is copied verbatim into the report for B: keep `fades.ts` as it is. The `ArrangementClip.tsx` gesture code has been the owner file three rounds running, and a per-kind handler table is proposed for a later checkpoint only.

**Things for C and B to know:**
- The first page load after my edits showed "Invalid hook call" and a hydration error from a Vite dependency rebuild; every later load was clean. C should do one warm-up load before the hydration row.
- I ran the mutations in place while the shared dev server was up, so for a few seconds it may have served a mutated file. Every file was restored byte-identical.
- Still open:
  - the full browser acceptance of task §5, at both viewports, is C's;
  - fades can't be edited from the keyboard;
  - near a clip's right edge, the fade-out ramp line sits about 2 px off its handle;
  - SRW-18 stage 2 (the clip volume envelope) is not started.
